preamble: Nasal assimilation of the voiced labial fricative [v] to [m] before a following nasal. In Old Norse, the cluster fn was pronounced with a voiced labial fricative before [n]; in Swedish and in Norwegian Nynorsk this fricative assimilated in nasality to the following [n], giving mn: Old Norse hǫfn 'harbour' > Swedish and Nynorsk hamn, jafn 'even' > Swedish jämn, Nynorsk jamn. Danish and Norwegian Bokmål instead keep v (havn, jevn), and Icelandic has [pn].

examples.note: Old Swedish spellings hamn ~ hampn show the nasal outcome; Danish keeps havn.
Old Swedish iæmpn; compare Danish jævn, Icelandic jafn.
Old Swedish æfni with the fricative still written; the modern form has mn.
Bokmål has havn with the fricative kept.
